claims.text: Reinforcement-learning-based in-situ processing control can concurrently improve strength and ductility in metallic alloys.
Reinforcement-learning-based in-situ processing control can concurrently improve strength and ductility in other engineering materials.
The proposed method applies to materials in an as-processed or as-fabricated state.
The method is applicable under ambient or various operating conditions.
Reinforcement learning can optimize processing temperature, pressure, and deformation rate.
Adaptive adjustment of processing conditions through reinforcement learning produces optimal material properties.
Conventional materials processing involves a trade-off between strength and ductility.
Traditional alloy-design and processing-optimization methods have limitations that reinforcement-learning control can address.
A controlled comparison of reinforcement-learning-controlled processing with traditional processing can test the hypothesis.
